title: Error-Budget Marketplace and Capacity Brokerage Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the Error-Budget Marketplace (EBM) and Capacity Brokerage pattern for Redwood Inference: a lightweight, governed market for teams to trade error-budget credits and short-term capacity reservations. The marketplace aligns SLO-driven incentives with pragmatic capacity allocation during predictable surges and planned experiments while preserving reliability guardrails.

Audience and scope
-------------------
- Primary: SREs, platform engineers, service owners (model tenants)
- Secondary: Product engineering managers, capacity planners, solutions engineers
- Scope: multi-tenant inference clusters, Dedicated pools, and cross-region failover fabric. This playbook covers: marketplace model, ledger primitives, governance rules, automated broker API, human workflows for disputes, and integration points with observability and incident review.

Why we need an Error-Budget Marketplace
---------------------------------------
1. Predictable experiments and feature launches often cause temporary SLO pressure. A market lets teams purchase short-term headroom without permanent overprovisioning.
2. Operational transparency: credits are explicit, auditable, and tie to cost/accounting.
3. Encourages ownership: teams paying for credits will prefer graceful degradation strategies.
4. Enables SRE to reclaim capacity proactively when systemic risk rises, with minimal coordination friction.

Glossary
--------
- SLO: Service-level objective for a service or tenant (e.g., p99 latency & availability targets).
- Error budget credit (EBC): transferable unit representing 1% of a service-month of error budget at a given SLO target (see ledger examples).
- Capacity credit (CC): token representing reserved GPU/GPU-slice pool seconds or tokens for a specified QPS headroom for a window.
- Broker: automated service that matches buy/sell orders and enforces guardrails.
- Ledger: append-only audit log of EBC/CC transactions.

Principles and constraints
--------------------------
- Safety first: marketplace cannot be used to permanently reduce SLOs. Any trade must include an explicit rollback or expiry.
- SLA guardrails: critical tenant SLO tiers (tier-0) are not eligible to sell credits.
- Transparency: all transactions are logged and visible to finance and SRE.
- Chargeback: traded credits map to billing codes; finance reconciliation hooks required.
- Automation preferred: manual trades allowed only through a documented escalation path.

SLO and error-budget mapping to marketplace units
------------------------------------------------
- We standardize EBC as: 1 EBC = 1 percentage-point of monthly error budget for a named SLO. Example SLO: availability 99.95% for model-serving-route-a. If route-a has a monthly error budget of 0.05% (i.e., 99.95 target), then 1 EBC corresponds to a purchase that allows an additional 1% of budget usage (coverage proportional to current budget duration).

Ledger primitives (text table)
------------------------------
Each ledger line must include the following fields (CSV example shown):
- timestamp, tx_id, buyer, seller, unit_type (EBC|CC), unit_qty, sLO_name_or_pool, expiry_iso, approval_id, reason_note

Example CSV row:
2026-02-09T15:22:03Z, tx-9f3b, tenant-data-kg, platform-reserve, EBC, 3, p99-latency-modelX, 2026-02-09T23:59:59Z, apr-873, "Launch: 2h extra error budget for feature flag canary"

Operational guardrails and approval workflow
-------------------------------------------
1. Automatic pre-checks by Broker:
   - Verify seller is not a tier-0 or security-restricted tenant.
   - Ensure buyer's target SLO is compatible with purchased unit type.
   - Validate that expiry <= 30 days for EBCs and <= 7 days for CCs (configurable).
2. Soft-approval path (auto): orders under thresholds (EBC <= 5, CC <= 100 GPU-min) proceed automatically.
3. Manual escalation: anything exceeding thresholds or impacting >2 regions requires SRE lead review and approval_id.
4. Dispute resolution: disputes attach to ledger entries; SRE audit panel has 48h SLA to adjudicate.

Automation: Broker API and CLI
-----------------------------
We provide a broker REST API and a small CLI shim. All operations create ledger entries and emit telemetry to SLO-observability. Authentication uses the existing platform-service-account pattern (RBAC).

API examples (simplified)
POST /broker/v1/orders
Headers: Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}
Body (JSON as plain text):
{
  "buyer":"team-search",
  "seller":"platform-pool",
  "unit_type":"CC",
  "unit_qty":"60",
  "sLO_name_or_pool":"dedicated-gpu-pool-eastus-2",
  "expiry":"2026-02-15T04:00:00Z",
  "reason":"Traffic spike for marketing campaign - 4h reservation"
}

CLI example
-----------
# Request 4 GPU-min capacity credit for 2 hours
$ rdbx broker buy --unit CC --qty 120 --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-eastus-2 --expiry 2026-02-09T18:00:00Z --reason "canary launch"

Telemetry and observability integration
-------------------------------------
- Broker emits the following metrics (prometheus-style):
  - ebm_orders_total{result="accepted|rejected|escalated"}
  - ebm_open_credits{tenant="...", unit_type="EBC|CC"}
  - ebm_active_capacity_reserved_seconds
  - ebm_disputes_total
- Events are forwarded to the SLO observability pipeline and can be correlated with SLI rollups (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, error_rate).
- Dashboards: new EBM dashboard (per-tenant ledger view, active reservations, dispute queue, cost center mapping).

Integration points with incident review and error-budget processes
-----------------------------------------------------------------
- When an incident causes SLO consumption, the incident review template must include: any EBC/CC trades during the incident window, ledger tx_ids, and whether purchased credits materially changed remediation choices.
- Post-incident action owners should assess whether the marketplace allowed an avoidable bypass of long-term remediation; if yes, place remediation as a mandatory follow-up with a due date.

Runbook: routine operations (5-step quick start)
------------------------------------------------
1. Query ledger for open credits: rdbx broker ledger --tenant team-search --open
2. Validate telemetry: review ebm_open_credits and p99 latency behavior during reservation window.
3. If broker auto-approved a large order flagged by SLO anomalies, open an incident in PagerDuty with tag ebm-auto-approval.
4. If dispute raised, attach ledger export and assign to SRE audit panel (owner: service-steward-sre).
5. After expiry, reconcile credits to billing codes with finance via automated daily export (S3 /reports/ebm/daily).

Human workflows and governance cadence
------------------------------------
- Weekly: EBM health sync (SRE + capacity planning + finance) to reconcile major trades and identify recurring buyers.
- Monthly: Marketplace review — analyze top buyers, sellers, and any systemic patterns that indicate poor SLO design or repeated overreliance on marketplace credits.
- Quarterly: Policy refresh — adjust auto-approval thresholds, expiry windows, and pricing model.

Policy: pricing and incentives (example)
-------------------------------------
- Default pricing: 1 EBC = internal charge unit 100 (applies to chargeback and to discourage frivolous purchases).
- Discounts: long-running CC reservations (>7d) require SRE approval and are charged at higher internal rates to deter long-term capacity hoarding.
- Refunds: no refunds for EBCs after expiry. Dispute refunds only after SRE audit clearance.

Incident review checklist additions
---------------------------------
Add these items to incident postmortems when EBM was used in the incident window:
- Which ledger entries were active? (tx_ids)
- Who authorized the trades? (auto vs manual, approval_id)
- Could we have employed alternative mitigations (rate-limiting, canary rollback, model quantization)?
- Action item: For any trade that increased blast radius, schedule a remediation ticket with priority P1/P2 based on business impact.

Automation playbooks for SRE engineers
-------------------------------------
- Auto-abort: if overall platform SLOs degrade > 2x burn-rate within a rolling 15m window, broker automatically halts new orders and flags open CCs for immediate review.
- Emergency reclamation: SRE can invoke broker reclaim --tx tx-xxxx to preempt non-critical CCs with a documented evidence ID; reclaim triggers an automated notification to buyer and seller.

Template: ledger query CLI and CSV export
-----------------------------------------
# Export last 7 days for tenant
rdbx broker ledger --tenant team-search --from 2026-02-02 --to 2026-02-09 --format csv > team-search-ebm.csv
CSV columns: timestamp,tx_id,buyer,seller,unit_type,unit_qty,slo_or_pool,expiry,approval_id,reason

Safety and audit considerations
------------------------------
- Ledger retention: 7 years (for compliance and billing disputes).
- Auditability: every API call to the broker must include an actor_id and trace_id.
- Rate limits: per-tenant order rate limit default 10 orders/hour.
- Testing: all broker code changes must pass a chaos test suite that simulates concurrent trades and broker restarts.

Operational readiness checklist (pre-launch)
------------------------------------------
- [ ] Broker service deployed in canary region with integration to SLO-observability.
- [ ] Ledger export pipeline validated end-to-end to S3 and finance ingestion.
- [ ] Auto-approval thresholds tuned and approved by SRE lead.
- [ ] Dashboards and alerts created for ebm_orders_total and ebm_disputes_total.
- [ ] Incident review template updated to include EBM fields.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Broker owner: platform-capacity-team (primary oncall: @platform-capacity-oncall)
- SRE audit panel: service-steward-sre (rotation scheduled in Doodle calendar)
- Finance contact: Kate Liao (billing reconciliation)

Appendix: Example ledger snippet (JSON as text)
------------------------------------------------
[
  {
    "timestamp":"2026-02-09T15:22:03Z",
    "tx_id":"tx-9f3b",
    "buyer":"tenant-data-kg",
    "seller":"platform-reserve",
    "unit_type":"EBC",
    "unit_qty":"3",
    "sLO_name_or_pool":"p99-latency-modelX",
    "expiry_iso":"2026-02-09T23:59:59Z",
    "approval_id":"apr-873",
    "reason_note":"Launch: 2h extra error budget for feature flag canary"
  }
]

Questions and future work
-------------------------
- Tie-in with external chargeback (cloud provider credits) and cost-optimization to surface price signals to buyers.
- ML-driven recommendation engine: suggest CC vs EBC purchases based on historical SLI patterns.
- Evaluate gamification risks: monitor for adverse behaviors where teams intentionally trigger budget burn to resell credits.
